speaker: Mr David Ong
text: asked	the Minister for National Development (a) what is the number of rental applications received under the Public Rental Scheme over the past year and how many of these applications are under the Joint Singles Scheme; and (b) how many complaints has HDB received of disputes among residents under the Joint Singles Scheme in the past two years.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked	the Minister for National Development whether HDB will consider implementing a pilot scheme for rental flats where single tenants are allowed to rent a smaller rental flat instead of requiring a minimum of two co-tenants.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: JSS ensures prudent use of limited public rental flats to help those in need.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Most JSS tenants are able to live together amicably.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, there are instances where tenants are unable to get along and request for a change of tenant.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In such cases, HDB will advise them to settle their dispute amicably or seek help from the grassroots organisations or the Community Mediation Centre.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: If the dispute cannot be settled and one person needs to move out, HDB will advise the remaining person to include another eligible single to retain the flat.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The outgoing person may submit a fresh application to rent another public rental flat with another eligible person.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Nonetheless, since 2015, HDB has made available some new 1-room rental flats with partitions to create separate sleeping areas for each occupant, for singles who prefer more privacy.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Each sleeping area can accommodate a single bed and a small wardrobe and has its own windows, while the living area, kitchen and toilet remain shared.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For those who need to stay alone for exceptional reasons, such as medical grounds, HDB will assess their requests on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: A few supplementary questions: first, how effective is the HDB's current mediation framework in helping to resolve such disputes between co-tenants, because I do see quite frequent cases of co-tenants having disputes and having difficulties coping?

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: The next question is: some of the flats under JSS are currently occupied by only one tenant instead of two.

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: What actions is HDB taking to ensure that such flats are prudently and optimally rented out?

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: My last question: although there is now the option of a rental flat with a partition, will HDB consider other rental flat options for singles, so as to reduce such conflicts of strangers living together?

speaker: Mr David Ong (Bukit Batok)
text: Perhaps, more of such schemes can be expanded to give more privacy to singles – maybe a single unit with shared toilets and cluster living options.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In cases of difficulty getting along, we will usually allow some time for the Residents' Committees, local grassroots as well as the Community Mediation Centre to mediate between the two tenants and hope for a good resolution.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In cases where the tenants cannot get along, we would usually not force such pairings and may exercise some flexibility but we would usually seek an approach in which we encourage the tenants to continue to look for an eligible partner with whom they can get along to share the flat with.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand he has answered my question and said that MND has no plans to carry out a pilot scheme for smaller rental flats where tenants can live alone.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I am sure for most of us here, we have met residents who just cannot get along with their co-tenant, to the extent that they suffer from depression and it affects their mental and health well-being, even after attempts to mediate.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am interested in the scheme that the Minister of State mentioned, the new 1-room rental flats with partitions.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How many of such flats have been introduced, what are the areas where such flats have been introduced and are there plans to introduce such flats with partitions to more areas in our housing estates?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: HDB does exercise flexibility in each of the cases where there is difficulty in people getting along and staying Page: 31 together within the same rental flat.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the question on whether we would be building more of such unique 1-room rental flats, from the 2012 Building Plan onwards, certain stacks of 1-room flats are designed where feasible, with dual windows and partition walls.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The partitions will divide the bed area into two with the living area, kitchen and the toilets as the common amenities.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Each bed area will have sufficient spaces, as I had said earlier, to accommodate a bed as well as a small wardrobe, so that there is some degree of privacy for the tenants within a 1-room configuration.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Starting from some projects under the 2013 Building Plan, such 1-room flats are further designed with partitions and doors that compartmentalise the sleeping areas such that each occupant will have a semblance of his or her own bedroom.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State for greater granularity, as to how many were for medical exceptions and how many were for other circumstances?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I do not recall that a number was provided for those who are currently staying alone but not evicted because they have difficulty getting along with fellow tenants.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Is there a number to that and does the Minister of State feel that this could become a potential issue?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: That is, if I want to stay alone, I just be very difficult with my co-tenants and I will, therefore, have the flat to myself?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Please keep your reply short, Minister of State.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Perhaps we could take this as a separate Parliamentary Question in subsequent Sittings.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.] Page: 32
